blocks.text: **Biotechnology** uses living organisms/systems to make products and processes, while **nanotechnology** manipulates matter at the **atomic/molecular (nano) scale**. Both are transformative across health, agriculture, industry and the environment.

rows: Vaccines, insulin, gene therapy, diagnostics, monoclonal antibodies.
1–100 nm scale; drug delivery, nano-materials, electronics, water purification.
**DBT (Dept of Biotechnology); BIRAC; nano — Nano Mission**.

items: **Biotechnology** = using living systems for products/processes; branches — **red** (medical: insulin, vaccines, gene therapy), **green** (agri: Bt crops, GM), **white** (industrial: enzymes, biofuels), **blue** (marine).

**Applications**: recombinant vaccines (Covid — Covaxin/Covishield), **CRISPR gene editing**, monoclonal antibodies, stem cells, biofertilisers, tissue culture, DNA fingerprinting (forensics), biopharma.
**Nanotechnology** = manipulating matter at 1-100 nm; applications — drug delivery, water purification, stronger/lighter materials, electronics, sensors, textiles, agriculture (nano-fertilisers).
**Institutions**: **DBT, BIRAC, Biotechnology parks**; **Nano Mission**; India's biotech economy is fast-growing; **Genome India** project.

sections.heading: Ethical, social & legal issues & government policies

blocks.text: Biotechnology raises **ethical, social and legal (ELSI)** concerns — over GM foods, biosafety, gene editing, data privacy and equity — regulated in India by a framework of **biosafety rules and regulatory bodies**.

rows: GM-food safety, gene editing of humans, cloning, designer babies, consent.
Biopiracy, farmers' rights, IPR/patents on life, biosafety.
**Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee** — approves GMO release (under MoEFCC).
**Biosafety rules (1989); proposed biotech regulator; Cartagena Protocol** (biosafety).

sections.heading: 🧬 Exam-ready deep coverage: bioethics, law & policy

items: **Ethical/social/legal issues**: GM-crop safety & biosafety (Bt brinjal moratorium; Bt cotton allowed; GM mustard debate), gene-editing of humans, cloning, surrogacy, data privacy of genomes, biopiracy (neem/turmeric/basmati patent battles).

**Regulation**: **GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee)** clears GMOs; **Biological Diversity Act 2002 / NBA** (access & benefit-sharing, anti-biopiracy); **Drugs & Cosmetics rules, ICMR bioethics guidelines**; **Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021, ART Act 2021**.
**Global**: **Cartagena Protocol** (biosafety), **Nagoya Protocol** (ABS), Convention on Biological Diversity.
**Balance**: innovation & food security vs safety, equity & environment.

sections.heading: Genetic engineering — issues & impact on human life, health & environment

blocks.text: **Genetic engineering** directly modifies an organism's **DNA** to achieve desired traits. It powers advances in **medicine, agriculture and industry** — but its impact on **human health, the environment and ethics** is closely debated.

rows: **Recombinant DNA, PCR, gene cloning, CRISPR-Cas9 (gene editing)**.
**Gene therapy, insulin/vaccines, genetic diagnosis, personalised medicine**.
**GM crops** (pest/drought resistance, higher yield, biofortification — Golden Rice).
Gene flow to wild species, loss of biodiversity, superweeds/pests.

sections.heading: 🧬 Exam-ready deep coverage: genetic engineering — impact

items: **Genetic engineering** = directly altering DNA (recombinant DNA, **CRISPR-Cas9**, gene therapy, cloning).
**Health**: gene therapy for inherited diseases, personalised medicine, recombinant insulin/vaccines, mRNA vaccines; risks — off-target edits, designer-baby ethics, germline editing.
**Agriculture**: GM crops (pest-resistant Bt, herbicide-tolerant, biofortified — Golden Rice with vitamin A); benefits — yield, nutrition; concerns — biodiversity, gene flow, corporate seed control.
**Environment**: bioremediation (microbes cleaning pollutants), biofuels; but ecological risks of releasing GMOs.
**Regulation**: GEAC, biosafety norms, ethical oversight — the innovation-vs-precaution debate.

prelimsPointers: **Recombinant DNA technology** = combining DNA from different sources (genetic engineering).
